title: Cohort-aware rollback signal composer and sensitivity tuner
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Implement a cohort-aware signal composer that aggregates multiple SLO signals (latency percentiles, client-visible error-rate, token cost per 1k, and throughput) into a single calibrated rollback score. The feature will allow retention of per-cohort baselines (by customer tier, model family, request context-length bracket) and apply sensitivity maps so thresholds can be tuned per-cohort rather than globally. This reduces noisy rollbacks for low-volume customers and improves protection for high-value cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New 'rollback_score' metric emitted for every canary evaluation with breakdown by cohort; 2) Dashboard shows per-cohort baselines and historical sensitivity curves; 3) Automated rollback trigger can be configured to use cohort thresholds (absolute or z-score) and respects canary traffic weighting; 4) End-to-end test that injects latency/error/cost regressions and validates rollback fires within configured window; 5) Documentation and runbook updated.
design_decisions: We will keep the signal composition modular: each atomic signal (latency_p50/p95/p99, error_rate, token_cost_per_1k, throughput_rps) is normalized to a z-score against the cohort baseline, then combined using configurable weights into the rollback_score. Default weights favor p95 and error_rate. Baselines are updated via an exponentially weighted moving average with TTL and a robustness clamp to avoid drift during incidents. We rejected a single global threshold because it overtriggers for low-volume cohorts and underprotects enterprise tiers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: backend spike and simulation in staging (2 weeks). Phase 1: emit metrics in staging and enable read-only composer for dashboards (1 week). Phase 2: run closed canaries for internal test customers (10% traffic) and tune sensitivity maps (2 weeks). Phase 3: opt-in public canaries with automated rollback enabled for a subset of customers (configurable by project/organization) and monitoring for false positives (2 weeks). Phase 4: GA and default cohort baselines for enterprise plans (post-tuning).
metrics_signals:
- latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms)
- error_rate: client-visible 4xx/5xx and internal inference errors (counts and rates)
- token_cost_per_1k: aggregated token consumption cost for that cohort
- throughput: requests-per-second and queueing/backpressure indicators
- rollback_score: composed z-score (unitless)
tuning_strategy: 1) Run synthetic regressions to generate labeled positive/negative rollback events and build a ROC curve for the composed score. 2) Create sensitivity maps per cohort (e.g., enterprise, mid-market, free) and for model families (small/medium/large). 3) Provide two presets: conservative (high specificity) and protective (high sensitivity). 4) Offer an automated calibration job that suggests thresholds based on historical false-positive/false-negative trade-offs and expected cost of missed regression. 5) Allow manual overrides via Console feature flags.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for z-score normalization and weight composition.
- Integration test that simulates a 40% latency regression and validates rollback_score crosses threshold and triggers the rollback webhook.
- Chaos test: delayed KV cache invalidation to ensure signal robustness.
- Load test: ensure composer adds <2% p95 overhead under peak canary load.
- Canary observation: run for 48h and compare rollback events vs. manual annotations.
